# AI-friendly output

Canofold generates machine-readable files together with the site. The build does not call an external model and does not require an API key.

## Generated files

:::file-tree
- .canofold/
  - dist/
    - llms.txt
    - llms-full.txt
    - ai/
      - manifest.json
      - index.md
      - pages.json
      - summaries.json
      - code-examples.json
      - content/
        - current/
          - en/
            - 0001.jsonl
    - guide/
      - getting-started/
        - index.html
        - index.md
    - zh/
      - guide/
        - getting-started/
          - index.html
          - index.md
:::

| File | Contents | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `llms.txt` | Titles and site URLs selected by `ai.versions` | Crawler entry point |
| `llms-full.txt` | Full Markdown while within budget; otherwise a pointer to the shard manifest | Compatible entry point for small and large sites |
| `ai/manifest.json` | Schema version, budgets, totals, partitions, shard paths, sizes, record counts, and SHA-256 fingerprints | Stable discovery for complete corpora |
| `ai/content/{version}/{locale}/*.jsonl` | Size-bounded content records with `part` / `parts` | Streaming RAG ingestion without a monolithic download |
| `ai/index.md` | Page links; HTML routes when Markdown mirrors are disabled | Generic Markdown index |
| `ai/pages.json` | Routes, locales, heading trees, tags, owners, frontmatter, and timestamps | Metadata before RAG chunking |
| `ai/summaries.json` | Deterministic page summaries | Result previews and route filtering |
| `ai/code-examples.json` | Routes, locales, and fenced code | Code-example search |
| Per-page `index.md` | Markdown or MDX source emitted when `markdownMirror` is enabled | Page-level retrieval and citation |

## Summary generation

Canofold makes no network request for summaries. It uses, in order:

1. Frontmatter `description`.
2. The first body paragraph that is not a heading or code block.
3. An empty string when no suitable paragraph exists.

Write a precise `description` for every public page instead of a promotional slogan.

## Inclusion rules

- Published pages in the current version are included by default.
- Historical versions are excluded to avoid multiple outdated answers for the same topic.
- Pages with `status: draft` can be previewed and checked locally, but are omitted from production builds.
- `ai: false` excludes a page.
- `tags` and `owner` are preserved in `pages.json`.

```yaml
---
title: Internal incident response
description: Incident steps for the private network
ai: false
---
```

## Configuration

```ts
export default {
  markdownMirror: true,
  ai: {
    pageIndex: true,
    fullContent: true,
    llmsTxt: true,
    llmsFullTxt: true,
    markdownIndex: true,
    pageSummaries: true,
    codeExamples: true,
    chunkSizeBytes: 262144,
    llmsFullMaxBytes: 10485760,
    llmsFullOverflow: 'manifest',
    versions: 'current'
  }
}
```

Per-page Markdown mirrors, `pages.json`, and versioned full-content shards have independent switches and are enabled by default. Other files follow their own switches. With Markdown mirrors disabled, `ai/index.md` links to HTML routes and AI records omit `markdownPath`. A content record never exceeds `chunkSizeBytes`; an unusually large page is split on
Unicode code-point boundaries and reconstructed in `part` order. When the full corpus exceeds
`llmsFullMaxBytes`, `manifest` keeps `llms-full.txt` small and points to the lossless shards, while
`error` fails the atomic build. `versions: 'all'` includes historical snapshots in isolated
version/locale partitions; `current` remains the safer default.

If `ai.fullContent` is disabled and `llms-full.txt` exceeds its budget, the `manifest` overflow policy also fails the build rather than linking to a nonexistent shard manifest.

## Machine-consumption contract in 0.7.0

Canofold 0.7.0 uses schema 2. Older 0.6.x manifests use schema 1; upgrade the producer and reader before relying on these fields.

The page index and full manifest share `schemaVersion: 2`, `scope`, `outputs`, `basePath`, `snapshotRevision` and `pages`. The manifest includes its own inventory and works with the index disabled. When enabled, `pageIndex` declares its path, byte size and SHA-256; its snapshot and inventory must match the manifest.

| Field | Meaning for consumers |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Identity derived from content space, version, locale and locale-relative source path, independent of deployment URLs |
| `revision` | Revision of content facts and representation; title/body edits retain identity |
| `source.path` / `source.kind` | Logical source and Markdown/MDX kind; paths use `/` and Unicode NFC, without local absolute paths |
| `source.revision` / `source.transformedRevision` | SHA-256 of the authored file and complete Extension-transformed source |
| `representation.body` | `extension-transformed-source-body`, retaining author syntax |
| `representation.facts` | `compiled-static-with-author-and-extension-overrides`, compiled facts with author/Extension overrides |
| `representation.analysis` | `markdown-static` or `mdx-static-only`; runtime MDX output is outside the static guarantee |
| `representation.fingerprint` | UTF-8 SHA-256 of the reconstructed body |
| `representation.declaredInputsRevision` | Declared plugin/Extension input fingerprint, not arbitrary executable code or environment identity |

Set `ai.contentSpace: 'my-project'` when the same collection must move across roots or hosts. Omission yields `scope.space: null`, allowing comparison only within the same source root. Names contain 1–200 ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens and start with a letter or digit. A namespace is a publisher declaration, not authentication.

JSONL records use `documentId` to reference pages and `part`/`parts` for reconstruction. Validate sizes, fingerprints, record counts, version/locale, unique parts and body fingerprints before committing consumer state. An absent baseline, missing shard, failed request, corruption or unsupported format must not delete old records.

A source move creates an exit and an addition; title/body edits preserve identity. `ai: false`, drafts, source deletion and version selection can all remove a document from the AI collection; absence alone does not prove source deletion. Disabled outputs are neither content deletion nor access control. A complete consumer snapshot differs from the historical-directory `canofold snapshot` command.

Markdown mirrors retain complete Extension-transformed source. JSONL and full `llms-full.txt` retain its parsed body; none is serialized from HTML. Plugins can change compiled headings and summaries independently of source syntax. Select the appropriate representation and treat retrieved MDX/instructions as data.

Upgrade all Canofold packages and the reader together, rebuild and establish a new baseline when moving from schema 1. Do not interpret a format reset as mass additions/deletions. See [Skills](/en/skills/) for the reading workflow and failure handling.

### Independent reader example

Get the complete `canofold-knowledge-reader` Skill directory matching 0.7.0 and run its reference script with Node.js 22 or newer. It reads public files without importing Core or executing retrieved MDX:

```sh
node path/to/canofold-knowledge-reader/scripts/read-page.mjs .canofold/dist /guide/
node path/to/canofold-knowledge-reader/scripts/read-page.mjs https://docs.example.com/project/ /project/guide/
node path/to/canofold-knowledge-reader/scripts/read-page.mjs .canofold/dist --snapshot
node path/to/canofold-knowledge-reader/scripts/read-page.mjs .canofold/dist --snapshot --previous trusted-snapshot.json
```

Replace `/guide/` with an actual indexed `routePath`; remote roots must include their deployment prefix. Without a baseline, `changes.status` is `unknown`. Save a new snapshot only after a successful command returns `complete: true`, retaining old state on failure. The default entry is the full manifest. With only an index, `--snapshot --index` returns metadata, not body evidence. This is a runnable reference implementation, not a separate npm SDK.

## Private documentation

AI files and neighboring Markdown sources are static site output. An access layer for a private site must protect `/*.md`, `/ai/*`, `/llms*.txt`, and search indexes as well as HTML pages.
